triggers.description: Explicit sensory explanation or rendition of software or architecture, including an already understood system.
exclusions: literal syntax or output-shape request without sensory intent
literal appearance description without cross-modal intent

triggers.description: Compare alternatives using stable sensory correspondences grounded in common technical axes.
exclusions: ordinary optimization wording without sensory intent or representational ambiguity

triggers.description: Concrete competing structural, temporal, interaction, or boundary interpretations may benefit from sensory recoding or a better discriminator.
exclusions: generic uncertainty with no competing interpretations
ordinary domain work already clear literally and no explicit sensory request

triggers.description: An owning workflow identifies a concrete representational ambiguity that cross-modal recoding may clarify.
exclusions: generic architecture task with no ambiguity
generic performance task with no ambiguity
generic readability task with no ambiguity

triggers.description: Explicit durable endorsement, correction, rejection, retraction, reopening, or mapping/boundary instruction; alternatively accepted operational use in two independent contexts with demonstrated utility.
exclusions: mere repetition without accepted operational use

routes.description: Explore sensory representations to generate or distinguish technical hypotheses and discriminating tests.
Render a coherent sensory experience with recoverable engineering correspondences and limits; no unresolved defect is required.
Compare alternatives on stable sensory and technical axes without aesthetic rigging.
Return route-shaping sensory insight and a literal next move to the implementation owner.
Capture one qualifying canonical event, then transport its accepted derived admission when warranted; retain separate outcomes.
Use literal handling when there is no sensory intent or useful representational ambiguity; not a veto on explicit rendition.
Report missing evidence, custody, authority, or prior identity without invalidating independent completed work.

required_artifacts: literal evidence, supplied architecture, or explicit not-inspected boundary
success_signals: explicit sensory architecture requests do not require a bug or competing diagnosis
ordinary technical work retains its owner
a concurrent durable event is handled under SYN-MEMORY-003 without rerunning the sensory pass
failure_signals: activation solely because ordinary work mentions architecture, performance, readability, flakiness, UX, handoff, or closeout
keyword matching overrides a literal syntax request
explicit rendition is declined merely because literal explanation is sufficient
memory admission without its independent gate
clauses.rationale: Sensory intent and concrete representational need govern activation, not broad domain ownership.

required_artifacts: recoverable engineering meaning for material sensory claims
limits and omitted relations for explanation
uncertainty and falsifier or discriminating test for material diagnostic claims
explanation, comparison, investigation, or route delta
success_signals: representations may discover hypotheses before a finished technical translation
task-relative accountability does not demand lossless isomorphism
independent modalities may jointly answer one question
a missing measurement is identified rather than fabricated
failure_signals: several modalities restate the same claim
explanatory imagery requires an irrelevant experimental falsifier
minimum output becomes a cap on useful exploration
clauses.rationale: Explore representations freely; validate claims according to their use.

required_artifacts: durable authority, narrow scope, and actual source references
canonical sensory payload and prior relationship when required
canonical transaction receipt and exact SYN identity on success
derived admission disposition and actual MSN proof when admitted
resolved note relationships with preserved canonical provenance
digest status or explicit non-rollback warning when applicable
success_signals: explicit durable authority needs no repetition
two-context accepted operational use can qualify without an explicit durability phrase
canonical capture happens once and its returned identity is reused
local-only canonical success does not require a global note or digest
canonical and note identities are not substituted without exact correspondence
mixed explanatory and durable requests complete both eligible parts
successful admissions retain source note IDs and refresh their digest
failure_signals: qualifying capture is only described, not attempted
SYN relationships are passed as if they were MSN relationships
missing prior admissions cause guessed IDs or automatic backfill
canonical success is rolled back or reported failed because admission or digest failed
source notes or canonical history are silently rewritten or relocated
clauses.rationale: Canonical capture, derived admission, and materialized views have distinct identities, authority, and success conditions.

required_artifacts: actual sensory representation when supported by the artifact
nearby engineering correspondences and important limits
success_signals: architecture remains perceptible through space, sound, rhythm, motion, texture, contrast, or pressure
requested richness is preserved without redundant modalities
existing structure can justify an explanation without an action list
failure_signals: the requested sensory experience is replaced by technical paraphrase
sensory richness is treated as inherently unrigorous
examples become a fixed universal property-to-sensation dictionary
clauses.rationale: Preserve architecture-to-senses translation as a first-class capability, not decorative output or a diagnosis-only permission.

instrumentation.rationale: Use relevant routing probes, canonical receipts, and immutable source-note evidence; do not introduce a runtime reporting ritual.
